text:
matt: Heads-up — CI artifacts for the new attention_tiled kernels jumped ~7.2MB on linux release build, noticed in the nightly toolchain job.

build-bot: [artifact-size-check] /artifacts/attention_tile/fatbin.so = 32.1MB (baseline 24.9MB) — size-threshold-exceeded

raj: Oof. Do we have the exact nvcc command line from the build? suspect extra PTX/CUBIN inclusion from gencode entries.

katie: Pasting the compile step we run in the build: 
```
nvcc -O3 -Xcompiler "-fPIC" -rdc=true \
  -gencode arch=compute_80,code=compute_80 \
  -gencode arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 \
  -lineinfo -Xptxas "-v" -lcudart -o lib/attention_tile.fatbin.so objs/*.o
```

katie: The compute_80 code=compute_80 line emits PTX, and the code=sm_80 emits cubin. Both get packaged into the fatbin -> bigger file.

matt: Right — we added the tiled kernels and left both lines for fallback. That explains the jump.

jen: We intentionally keep PTX for driver fallback and forward-compatibility. If we strip PTX we could lose ability to run on future GPU archs without recompiling.

raj: Tradeoff: runtime size vs driver fallback. For hosted/Dedicated builds maybe we can drop PTX if we pin target hardware; for Private we should keep PTX. Need a clear policy.

katie: Proposal: default CI uses size-constrained release (no compute PTX entries) and a separate compatibility build (with PTX) that is allowed bigger. Also add a CI gate that fails if any fatbin grows > +10% unless a compat-build label is present.

matt: Sounds reasonable. We should also try minor build tweaks before removing PTX: 1) enable --compiler-options "-fvisibility=hidden" 2) use objcopy/strip on host symbols 3) ensure -rdc=false when not needed to avoid device-reloc overhead.

raj: Quick experiment: ran nvcc with -rdc=false and removed compute (PTX) entry locally — artifact went from 32.1MB -> 25.3MB. So most of the growth was PTX + rdc relocations.

katie: Another trick: change gencode from separate compute+sm entries to single code=sm_80; nvcc will still emit PTX for non-target if you explicitly set keep option, but default is smaller.

jen: Reminder: some customers use fallback to older drivers, we should not silently break that. If we split CI this way, docs + release notes need to explain the compatibility build.

ci-bot: Proposed CI job changes: 
```
- job: artifact-size-check
  script: ./tools/check_fatbin_size.sh --max-percent=10 --baseline artifacts/baseline.json
  allow_failure: false
- job: compat-fatbin-build
  script: ninja compat-fatbin
  artifacts: paths: [artifacts/compat/*]
  allow_failure: true
```

ci-bot: check_fatbin_size.sh would parse cuobjdump --dump-fatbin /path | wc -c and compare to baseline.

matt: Please add a per-package whitelist in the script for known planned increases (e.g. attention_tiled).

raj: Also consider shipping compressed fatbins in the package (LZ4 at packaging time) — storage/network impact is separate from runtime memory. But cloud-hosted runtime unpacks at deploy time. Might be OK.

katie: Action items: 
- katie: prototype CI split and check_fatbin_size.sh (PR soon)
- raj: test -rdc=false build and ensure no linker regressions for other kernels
- jen: draft compatibility doc + release note blurb for customers (impact & opt-in)
- matt: add per-package whitelist and gating exceptions in CI config

matt: Thanks. If anyone hits blockers while reproducing locally ping me. Let's aim for the CI change + whitelist today to stop noisy failures. :thumbsup:

jen: FYI I filed a short RFC note on the compat tradeoffs and linked it in the PR description — added context for product/legal.

build-bot: [ci] attention_tiled PR #3245 triggered — size-check pending

matt: Closing loop — once PR lands we can rebaseline the nightly size thresholds for bundles that legitimately need PTX.

raj: One more note: different nvcc/nvptx versions produce different PTX headers which can inflate size; lock toolchain in compat build to the latest verified driver to avoid surprises.

katie: Yep — I will pin the compat job to CUDA 12.3 and add a comment about toolchain variance.

matt: Great. Thanks everyone.
